To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Injection of the NO releasing agent Sin-1 molarisdomine (Sin-1) or the glutamate receptor agonist N-methyl-D- aspartate (NMA) onto the dendritic field of hippocampal granule cells results in a biphasic regulation in the expression of CaMKII mRNA, with an initial increase in the level of mRNA at 1-6 h after injection, and a decrease 24 h after the injection; and

(1) NMDA and nitric oxide increase CaMKII alpha expression in the dentate gyrus; (2) the increase in CaMKII expression is transient; (3) CaMKII expression in granule cells is regulated by cGMP-dependent kinase; and (4) CaMKII is regulated by NMDA receptors and nitric oxide in the dentate granule cells.

the expression of the alpha subunit mRNA for Ca2+/calmulin-dependent protein kinase type II (CaMK II alpha) in granule cells of the dentate gyrus is regulated in a biphasic manner by NMDA receptor stimulation or nitric oxide release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nitric oxide (NO) in the hippocampus, and the regulation of gene expression by this molecule and its precursor L-arginine.
the molecular basis of synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus.
the mechanisms of long-term synaptic plasticity, in particular the role of nitric oxide in long-term potentiation.
